The energy of the emitted photon is  

E = 2.3393 eV.

Convert this to wavelength:

λ (nm) = 1240 (eV·nm) / E(eV) = 1240 / 2.3393 ≈ 5.3 × 10² nm ≈ 530 nm.

A wavelength of about 530 nm lies in the green region of the visible spectrum, so the dye fluoresces green light.

In fluorescence, the light that is absorbed must have a slightly higher energy (i.e., shorter wavelength) than the light that is emitted, because some energy is lost non-radiatively before emission (Stokes shift). Hence the dye must absorb light that is somewhat toward the higher-energy (shorter-wavelength) side of green, i.e. in the blue region of the spectrum.

Among the choices given, “Blue” is therefore the best match for the color of light that is absorbed.

Answer: D
